name: Two pages, two figures, and only a date to separate them
description: Retrieval returns both. Nothing in either text says it has been superseded — the only thing that distinguishes them is the publication date, which the agent has to actually read rather than assume from the order results came back in.
goal: Report the current headcount for Project Atlas as an artifact named 'report': an object with 'headcount' (the figure) and 'source' (the url you took it from). Where two pages disagree, the more recently published one is current. Do not average, reconcile or hedge between them, and do not report a figure no page states.

assertions.description: The subject chose to finish. Erroring leaves the run unjudged; stopping to ask a human fails here, because the material holds everything the task needs
The later page says 61. The earlier one says 84 and is first in the results, so taking the top hit gets this wrong
The stale figure appears nowhere in the report — not as the answer, and not hedged alongside the current one
The report names the page it actually took the figure from

coverage.note: Search returns the stale page first on purpose. The date is the only discriminator and it is in the response, so this measures whether the agent read the metadata rather than the ranking.
